concepts.concept: Boot ROM read data  the 32-bit word taken from the embedded boot ROM and returned on the bus
concepts.writers: rdata is written by the mem_access process at line 48: rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(boot_rom_size_index_c+1 downto 2)))) on the rising edge of clk_i (rising_edge at line 47); the source array mem_rom_c is a constant initialized at line 35; no other writers in this module.
concepts.observers: bus_rsp_o.data is driven from rdata when rden = '1' (line 64); bus_rsp_o.ack (line 65) and bus_rsp_o.err (line 66) are outputs but only bus_rsp_o.data exposes the ROM word contents.

confidentiality.reason: The ROM word stored in rdata is presented on the output port bus_rsp_o.data when rden = '1' (line 64), so an external observer can read the word and the integrator may treat that word as secret.

integrity.reason: rdata is updated on each rising clock from mem_rom_c indexed by bus_req_i.addr (assignment at line 48, clock at line 47) while bus_rsp_o.data can present rdata when rden = '1' (line 64), so the delivered word can change due to external address changes and is not blocked while in use.

availability.reason: rdata is assigned unconditionally from the internal mem_rom_c at the clock edge (line 48) so nothing external in this RTL can freeze the internal rdata update (only its exposure is gated).

undermined behavior.reason: bus_rsp_o.data has a single gated driver from rdata (line 64) and there is no alternate debug/test override or bypass for the ROM read path in the RTL.

concepts.concept: Read-response decision  the latched signal that enables returning data and drives the ack (rden)
concepts.writers: rden is reset to '0' when rstn_i = '0' (synchronous reset path in the bus_feedback process at line 58) and otherwise latched on the rising edge of clk_i from bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (assignment at line 60); no other writers.
concepts.observers: rden gates the data output at bus_rsp_o.data (used in the conditional on line 64) and is directly copied to bus_rsp_o.ack (line 65), so rden is observable externally via bus_rsp_o.ack (and affects bus_rsp_o.data).

confidentiality.reason: rden is copied directly to the external output bus_rsp_o.ack (line 65) and is the value written (by the requester), so the RTL returns the value to the writer and does not withhold it.

integrity.reason: rden is clocked from bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 60) and that latched value directly controls delivery and ack (lines 64-65), so external inputs can change rden while it is in use and affect operation.

availability.reason: The bus_req_i fields drive rden at line 60; clearing or holding stb/rw prevents rden from being set and thus prevents data/ack (blocking progress), so an external actor can stop responses.

undermined behavior.reason: rden has a single clocked driver in the bus_feedback process (assignment at line 60, reset at line 58) and there is no alternate debug/test override in the RTL.

concepts.concept: Requested address (the bus-provided address bits that select which ROM word is read)
concepts.writers: bus_req_i.addr is an input port (declared in the port list at line 23) driven externally (outside this module); the module does not write it and it is sampled/used to index mem_rom_c in the mem_access assignment at line 48.
concepts.observers: The address is not output directly, but it selects rdata (line 48) and so the returned bus_rsp_o.data (line 64) is derived from the requested address and can be observed externally; there is no direct readback of the address itself.

confidentiality.reason: bus_req_i.addr is used to index ROM at line 48 and the selected ROM word is presented on bus_rsp_o.data (line 64), so observing the returned word can reveal which address was requested and the integrator may treat the address as sensitive.

integrity.reason: The ROM index is taken directly from bus_req_i.addr in the mem_access write to rdata (line 48) and that address is supplied by an external writer, so the integrity of the address depends on whether the external writer is trusted.

availability.reason: Returning a read requires the request handshake (rden set from bus_req_i.stb and not bus_req_i.rw at line 60); if stb is not asserted the module will not present data for any address, so external signals can block progress.

undermined behavior.reason: bus_req_i.addr is the single input used to select the ROM index at the mem_access assignment (line 48) and there is no alternate debug/test override in the RTL.
